messages:
Miguel: Hey team — new hire Miguel here. Just got the company Keychron K8 and it's paired via Bluetooth to my MacBook but keystrokes feel delayed (~200-400ms) and occasionally drop. Wired USB mode is fine. Any known quirks or quick fixes?
Priya: welcome Miguel :wave: can you confirm macOS version and whether you used the built-in BT or a dongle? also did you accept the pairing prompt fully (some models ask for a numeric code)?
Miguel: macOS Ventura 13.6, using built-in Bluetooth. Yes I accepted the prompt. It pairs but typing lag is noticeable.
it-bot: created ticket INC-5621 for Miguel (priority: medium) — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-5621
Jae: two quick checks: 1) try a clean unpair + restart Bluetooth: open System Settings -> Bluetooth -> Forget device, then restart and re-pair. 2) test with a wired USB-C cable to rule out keyboard firmware vs host.
Miguel: tried wired again just now — zero lag. So seems BT-specific. Did the forget/re-pair too, lag still there.
Priya: ok thanks. can you run this in Terminal and paste output? `system_profiler SPBluetoothDataType` and `log show --predicate 'process == "blued"' --last 1h | tail -n 30` — just to see any connection errors.
Miguel: pasted snippets (redacted) in the ticket. No obvious errors but I see repeated "IOBluetoothSDPServiceRecord" warnings.
Monica: sometimes macs have Bluetooth interference from 2.4GHz devices (mice, Wi-Fi). Do you have a USB-C dock or external Wi-Fi dongle near the keyboard?
Miguel: I'm on our office AP (2.4/5G) and my mouse is Bluetooth. I can try moving mouse to test.
Jae: also try disabling AWDL for a quick test: `sudo /usr/sbin/softwareupdate --background-critical` (jk) — actually run `sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.bluetoothd.plist ControllerPowerState -int 0; sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.bluetoothd.plist ControllerPowerState -int 1` to cycle hardware (you may need sudo). If uncomfortable, just reboot SMC/PRAM.
Priya: one more thing — some Keychron firmware has a reported issue where BT mode falls back to a low-power polling rate. There's a vendor firmware updater on Keychron's site. Miguel, before updating, check with Miguel’s manager if allowed; otherwise we can push via MDM.
Miguel: manager ok to update. Where's the firmware and do we keep layout/macros?
Monica: firmware: https://www.keychron.com/pages/download (link) — update preserves layout but you might need to re-pair. We'll coordinate: I can remote into your device via Jamf session and run the updater if you approve.
Miguel: please do that — jamf session scheduled in 10m. thanks! :thumbsup:
Priya: noted on the ticket — tagging Eng if we see similar across new hires. @Jae @Monica please add any follow-ups to INC-5621.
Jae: if firmware doesn't fix it, try creating a fresh macOS user and test Bluetooth there; helps rule out user-level kexts/settings.
Miguel: remote session went well, firmware updated, re-paired. Seems fixed! typing latency gone. thanks everyone :tada:
Priya: awesome — closing the loop. marking INC-5621 resolved and adding a short KB: "Keychron K8 — Bluetooth lag on macOS: update firmware, unpair/re-pair, check interference". Will push KB link in a bit.
Monica: adding note to new-hire checklist: if keyboard lag on BT, offer wired fallback + firmware update step.
Miguel: thanks all — super fast help :heart:
Priya: welcome to Redwood :raised_hands:
